Clinical details: Motorcyclist v car at approx. 40 mph, thrown from bike. Helmeted. Left upper quadrant tenderness. HR 112, BP 104/68. Trauma call.

Technique: Non-contrast CT head and cervical spine, followed by contrast-enhanced CT chest, abdomen and pelvis (split-bolus arterial/portal venous phase). Multiplanar bone reformats.

Head:
No intracranial haemorrhage or extra-axial collection. No midline shift. No skull vault or skull base fracture. Grey-white differentiation preserved.

Cervical spine:
No acute fracture or malalignment of the cervical spine. Craniocervical junction intact. Prevertebral soft tissues not thickened.

Chest:
Undisplaced fractures of the left 9th, 10th and 11th ribs posterolaterally. No flail segment. Small focus of contusion in the posterior basal left lower lobe adjacent to the fractures. No pneumothorax or haemothorax. Mediastinum not widened; no mediastinal haematoma and no traumatic aortic injury. No sternal or clavicular fracture.

Abdomen:
Splenic laceration at the lower pole extending 4 cm into the parenchyma from the lateral surface, with a perisplenic haematoma. No active extravasation and no pseudoaneurysm. AAST grade III splenic injury. Moderate haemoperitoneum in the left upper quadrant, left paracolic gutter and pelvis. Liver, pancreas and adrenals unremarkable. Kidneys enhance symmetrically; no perinephric haematoma. No free gas.

Pelvis:
Pelvic ring intact. Haemoperitoneum in the pelvis as described above; no extraperitoneal pelvic haematoma. Bladder unremarkable.

Thoracolumbar spine:
No thoracolumbar spinal fracture. Alignment maintained.

Conclusion:
1. AAST grade III splenic injury with moderate haemoperitoneum. No active extravasation.
2. Undisplaced left 9th to 11th rib fractures with adjacent minor pulmonary contusion. No pneumothorax.
3. No other acute traumatic injury.

Preliminary findings relayed to the trauma team leader in CT at 22:07.
